basis: Intellectual disability, epilepsy and hypogonadism define MEHMO; clubfoot occurs in 30-79%. Nystagmus alone does not establish ocular damage.
Congenital macrothrombocytopenia; hearing loss, nephropathy and presenile cataracts each annotated 30-79%. Elevated liver enzymes alone do not establish hepatic damage.
Familial primary hyperparathyroidism with hypercalcemia; bone loss is common (~30% or more). Separately diagnosed kidney stones are excluded.
Penile lichen sclerosus is an immune-mediated inflammatory and sclerosing skin disease. Urethral involvement is a minority complication.
Skeletal anomalies define syndrome; dental crowding/malocclusion 50-60%, conductive hearing loss 4/11, arrhythmia 3/9. Separately diagnosed sleep apnea excluded.
GRIN2B-related intellectual disability and neurodevelopmental dysfunction; non-neurologic abnormalities are uncommon.
Neuronal migration disorder with periventricular heterotopia, microcephaly, developmental impairment and seizures.
Umbrella for inborn peptide metabolism disorders; no additional damaged organ is established across most patients in the group.
Neurodevelopmental disorder; scoliosis 4/4, myopia 4/4 and sensorineural hearing loss 6/18. Patent ductus arteriosus 5/15 omitted because of the four-axis cap.
Familial restrictive cardiomyopathy directly affects myocardium; reported additional vascular abnormalities remain within the cardiovascular axis.
Mansonella nematode infection; pruritus, arthralgia and eosinophilia do not establish lasting organ damage. Skin disease varies by species.
Cutaneous vascular lesion occupying dermal/subcutaneous vessels with overlying epidermal hyperplasia and hyperkeratosis.
Microphthalmia, retinal degeneration and lens abnormalities define ocular disease; dental anomalies are also a defining feature.
Familial neurodegeneration with cerebral amyloid, neurofibrillary tangles and prion pathology; infectious transmission is not established by this diagnosis.
Infarction of cardiac septal myocardium; cardiac muscle belongs to the cardiovascular axis.
Defined by skeletal osteopoikilosis and cutaneous connective tissue nevi.
Congenital dilation of the ureter; ureters belong to the renal axis even without reflux or obstruction.
Combined immunodeficiency with defining optic and skeletal anomalies; developmental impairment, seizures and ataxia occur in 30-79%. Renal agenesis (30-79%) omitted by cap.
Pectus deformity and nail dysplasia define the syndrome despite lower HPO frequencies. Motor delay resolves in childhood; macrocephaly alone is not neurologic damage.
Bacterial infection directly causes myocardial inflammation.
Carcinoma originates in epidermal squamous cells; distant organ involvement is not typical across most patients.
Disease confined to the epididymis, a reproductive organ outside the thirteen axes.
Microphthalmia/coloboma and intellectual disability define syndrome; kyphoscoliosis occurs in 4/4 patients. Incisor spacing alone does not establish dental damage.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction causes chronic sinus and lung disease; recurrent middle-ear inflammation occurs in 6/6 patients. Situs inversus alone is not cardiac damage.
Inborn neurotransmitter transport disorder causing dystonia, parkinsonism and developmental impairment. Eye movements and nonspecific vascular findings do not establish separate organ damage.
